CNT forests with thickness >10 µm exhibit near-perfect absorption with absorptance and emittance close to 1.
CNT thicknesses of 0.36, 1.12, 4, 7, and 10 µm were achieved by varying CVD deposition times from 3 to 15 minutes.
The tandem absorber structure is SS/Ti/AlTiO/CoO/CNTs.
AlTiO layer forms due to outward diffusion of Ti during heat treatment at 800 °C.
CNTs grown at 0.36 µm thickness exhibit absorptance of 0.95 and emittance of 0.20, yielding a spectral selectivity ratio (α/ε) of 4.75.
Thermal stability of the CNT-based tandem absorber is maintained up to 650 °C for 100 hours in vacuum.
FESEM images show CNTs grown at different thicknesses are bent-interlinked forests rather than vertically aligned.
XRD confirms presence of graphitic carbon and cobalt oxide; alumina and titanium oxide layers are x-ray amorphous.
Raman spectra show high D/G intensity ratio (1.52) for as-grown CNTs indicating carbonaceous impurities; purified CNTs have ratio of 0.52.
The plasma edge (ωp) shifts from 544 nm for Co/Al2O3/Ti coated SS to 812 nm for CoO/AlTiO/Ti/SS, indicating changes in charge carrier density.
Complex refractive index of 10 µm thick CNTs shows low refractive index (~1.05) in 300–2200 nm range, aiding impedance matching to air.
Reducing CNT thickness increases reflectance in visible region due to higher reflection at CNT/air interface.
Transmittance measurements on CNTs grown on CoO/quartz substrates show decreased transmittance with increasing CNT thickness.
The CNT-based tandem absorber exhibits near-zero transmittance due to substrate opacity.
The absorptance and emittance were calculated from reflectance and transmittance using the relation A + R + T = 1 and Kirchhoff's law.
The CNT-based tandem absorber outperforms some state-of-the-art solar selective coatings that are stable up to 580 °C.
The CNT coatings have root mean square roughness values increasing from ~60 nm at 0.36 µm thickness to ~130 nm at 10 µm thickness.
The low effective refractive index of CNT forests results from their low volume fraction and high porosity.
The cobalt catalyst was chosen over Ni and Fe due to better optical absorption and thermal stability of CoO.
The CNT-based tandem absorber can be tuned to transition from broadband blackbody absorption to solar selective absorption by adjusting CNT thickness.
